name: Olfactory
description: Anything to do with the sense of smell. An 'olfactory family' is a group of scents that share a similar character, like citrus or woody.

name: Nose
description: The professional who composes perfumes. They train for years to recognize and combine thousands of raw materials.

name: Notes
description: The individual smells you can pick out in a perfume, like 'bergamot' or 'vanilla'. A note can be a real ingredient or an impression built from several.

name: Top Notes
description: What you smell first, in roughly the first 5-30 minutes. They're light and evaporate fastest, so they make the first impression.

name: Heart Notes
description: The main character of the perfume, appearing as the top notes fade and lasting a few hours. Often florals and spices.

name: Base Notes
description: The heaviest molecules that stay on skin longest, sometimes all day. Woods, resins, musks and vanilla usually live here.

name: Note Pyramid
description: A way to show how a perfume changes over time: top notes first, then heart, then base. It's a simplified guide rather than an exact recipe.

name: Accord
description: A blend of several ingredients that together create one new smell, like a musical chord. 'Leather accord' or 'amber accord' are common examples.

name: Sillage
description: The scent trail a perfume leaves behind you in a room (French for 'wake'). Strong sillage means people notice it as you walk past.

name: Longevity
description: How long a perfume lasts on your skin before you can no longer smell it. Depends on the ingredients, concentration and your skin.

name: Projection
description: How far the scent radiates from your body while you wear it. A perfume can last long but stay close to the skin.

name: Concentration
description: How much perfume oil is in the bottle, which affects strength and price. From lightest to strongest: Eau de Cologne, Eau de Toilette, Eau de Parfum, Parfum or Extrait.

name: Eau de Parfum
description: A concentration with about 15-20% perfume oil. Usually lasts 6-8 hours and is the most common strength for modern fragrances.

name: Eau de Toilette
description: A lighter concentration of about 5-15% perfume oil. Fresher and brighter, typically lasting 3-5 hours.

name: Extrait de Parfum
description: The richest concentration, about 20-40% perfume oil. Lasts longest and often smells deeper and smoother.

name: Eau de Cologne
description: The lightest classic concentration (2-5% oil), traditionally citrus-heavy and refreshing. In everyday English 'cologne' often just means men's perfume.

name: Absolute
description: A highly concentrated natural extract made with solvents, used for delicate flowers like jasmine that can't survive steam distillation. Smells very close to the real flower.

name: Essential Oil
description: A natural aromatic oil, usually extracted by steam distillation or pressing (like citrus peels). The traditional raw material of perfumery.

name: Aromachemical
description: A lab-made scent molecule. Synthetics let perfumers create smells nature can't give (like 'ozone' or 'lily of the valley') and replace animal or endangered materials.

name: Fixative
description: An ingredient that slows evaporation so a perfume lasts longer, often a base note like musk, resin or ambroxan.

name: Indole
description: A natural molecule in white flowers like jasmine that smells slightly animalic or even fecal on its own. In small amounts it makes florals feel alive and sensual.

name: Coumarin
description: A molecule found in tonka beans and fresh hay that smells sweet, warm and almondy. It's the key to the classic 'fougère' style.

name: Formaldehyde
description: A sharp, irritating chemical that isn't a perfume note at all. Some preservatives can release tiny amounts, which is why it shows up in ingredient-safety discussions.

name: Fougère
description: French for 'fern': a classic family built on lavender, oakmoss and coumarin. The backbone of many traditional barbershop-style men's scents.

name: Chypre
description: A classic family built on a citrus opening, a floral heart and a mossy, woody base (traditionally oakmoss). Feels elegant, dry and sophisticated.

name: Gourmand
description: A scent family that smells edible: vanilla, caramel, chocolate, coffee or praline. Sweet, cozy and dessert-like.

name: Oriental
description: An older name for the warm, spicy, resinous family now usually called 'Amber'. Think vanilla, resins and spices.

name: Animalic
description: Notes that smell warm, musky, skin-like or 'dirty', inspired by materials like civet or castoreum. Today they're almost always synthetic.

name: Powdery
description: A soft, dry, cosmetic-like effect, like face powder or baby powder. Iris, violet and heliotrope often create it.

name: Skin Scent
description: A perfume that sits close to the body and smells like 'your skin but better'. Usually soft musks and woods.

name: Flanker
description: A spin-off version of an existing perfume, like an 'Intense' or 'Elixir' edition. Same name family, different formula.

name: Blind Buy
description: Buying a perfume without smelling it first, based only on its notes and reviews. Risky but common in fragrance communities.

name: Decant
description: A small sample of perfume poured from a full bottle into a travel vial. A cheap way to try a scent before buying.

name: Maceration
description: The resting period after a perfume is mixed, when the ingredients blend and mature. Some people say a perfume smells better after a bottle has been open a while.

name: IFRA
description: The International Fragrance Association, which sets safety limits on perfume ingredients. Its rules are why some classic perfumes have been reformulated.

name: Reformulation
description: When a brand changes a perfume's formula, often due to new safety rules or costs. Fans often compare 'vintage' and current batches.

name: Niche
description: Perfumes from smaller, specialist houses that focus on artistry over mass appeal. Usually more unusual and more expensive than designer scents.

name: Designer
description: Perfumes from fashion brands like Dior, Chanel or Armani. Widely available and usually built to please many people.
